title: Auslander–Buchsbaum depth formula
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring (a ring with exactly one maximal ideal) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $M$ be a nonzero finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] of finite projective dimension [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Then $$\operatorname{depth}(R)=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}(M),$$ where depths are taken with respect to $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-depth].

proof.text: Let e be the least natural Ext projective-dimension bound supplied by finite projective dimension. Mathlib projectiveDimension_le_iff and projectiveDimension_ge_iff identify projectiveDimension M with e; nontriviality excludes bottom when e=0. The bounded-resolution comparison turns the minimum Ext bound into a resolution of length e. The module universe contains the ring universe.

Prove three private depth helpers in the restored Sheaf module: linear equivalences preserve depth by transporting regular sequences and the maximal-ideal quotient; a subsingleton module has infinite depth by definition; a finite free module has depth at least depth R by a finite basis, flat transport of regularity and Nakayama. The previously public Sheaf helpers were retired in favor of an upstream module whose helpers are private; no upstream visibility is changed.

For a length-e finite free resolution, factor each differential and the augmentation through its image. The degree-e map is injective because degree e+1 is zero. Write depth R=d using the Ext-depth theorem. Descending induction gives depth(im d_i) >= d-(e-i): apply the second depth inequality to 0 -> im d_(i+1) -> F_i -> im d_i -> 0. Images are finite as quotients of finite free terms. A zero right term has infinite depth; a zero left term makes the middle and right terms isomorphic, so the inequality remains valid without nonzero hypotheses. At i=0 the augmentation image is M. Thus d-e <= depth M and d <= e+depth M.

For an arbitrary finite module L with finite projective dimension q, use its minimum Ext bound and the bounded-resolution comparison and the minimal finite free resolution theorem. For q=0, q<=depth R is immediate. For q>0 a zero top term would give a shorter resolution and, by the comparison, a smaller Ext bound, so its rank is positive. Choose finite bases, transport the differential exactness and top injectivity to matrices. Minimality puts every coefficient in the maximal ideal; applying the residue quotient to each nonempty determinant shows its ideal is contained in the maximal ideal and is proper. The exact-free-complex last-minors lemma then gives a regular sequence of length q in that ideal, hence q<=depth R by the supremum definition.

Use finite depth from its Ext characterization and Nakayama to attain the finite supremum of lengths of M-regular sequences in the maximal ideal. Let rs have length t=depth M and Q=M/(rs)M, which is nonzero finite by regularity. Apply Mathlib ModuleCat.projectiveDimension_quotient_eq_add_length_of_isWeaklyRegular over the same ring R to obtain pd_R Q=pd_R M+t. The comparison in step 1 turns this finite dimension into an explicit resolution bound for Q. Apply step 4 to Q to get pd_R M+depth M<=depth R. Apply step 3 to a minimum-length finite free resolution of M for the reverse inequality and conclude by antisymmetry. This replaces the quotient-ring induction and its Tor comparison; the unit statements and realized steps are unchanged.

theorem depth_eq_projectiveDimension_add_depth
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Nontrivial M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (h : ModuleCat.HasFiniteProjectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R M)) :
    (depth (R := R) R : WithBot ℕ∞) =
      CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R M) +
        (depth (R := R) M : WithBot ℕ∞)
lean.note: Restore the quarantined proof against the canonical upstream finite-projective-dimension API. The equality is now in WithBot ℕ∞ and uses CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension. For the nonzero finite-dimensional module this equals the least natural Ext bound, which by the bounded-resolution bridge is the old least resolution length. No mathematical hypothesis or conclusion changes.
